# Local contributions and read-clock verification - 2026-10-20

Scope: local browser UI, disposable launcher/fixture, and production unsigned
approval preparation. No production Solidity changed; reused source-bound core
artifacts were authenticated by the launcher. Only the new native admission
fixture was compiled with Solidity 0.8.26 and the existing optimizer settings.

## Checks and observations

- 51 focused Python cases passed, then 18 supplemental cases passed after adding
  the reset-only/false-return case and final state capability response. These
  overlap: 52 distinct cases, not 69 independent tests. Includes monotonic expiry,
  chain resampling, fixed local $100 activation, decimal-aware exact approvals,
  atomic ETH, rejected legacy wrap flow and normal unsigned activation guards.
- 51 affected Node checks pass; JS syntax and website selector/artwork check pass.
- Browser: read-only activation amount is 100 local tokens, visibly $100 at the
  $1 mock price. Native ETH activation submitted one successful Entry transaction;
  PoPL #1 changed Dormant to Activated with $100 displayed attached LP.
- Browser: five USDC approval was followed automatically by the distinct Add
  attached LP review. Both confirmations stayed explicit. No third transaction,
  zero-reset or wrap occurred. Final displayed LP is $105.00; raw marked value
  is 104999999999999999999 due to one unit of share rounding. An initial probe
  expected >=105e18 and failed; inspection established this one-unit difference,
  which is retained here rather than treating display rounding as raw equality.
- [Sanitized local receipts and snapshot](local-observation.json) include other
  concurrent user rehearsal actions; they are not all assistant test actions.
- Existing 8896 fixture: all eight LP values available; full read 5.875 seconds.
  A single-NFT profiling comparison reduced clock reads from 1573 to four and
  elapsed time from 8.188 to 2.594 seconds. This is local observation, not SLA.
- Existing Anvil/NFTs/LP were preserved through web-only restarts. Separate
  native fixture on 8898, chain 31337. No public keys/funds or paused monitor used.

## Safety and limitations

Direct exact approval must simulate successfully (including ERC20 return value);
reset-only tokens fail closed instead of requiring a third send. Entry is an
owner-authenticated spender. Already sufficient allowance is reused, not revoked.
Approval itself does not deploy LP; each final Entry call is simulated again.
Lost responses recover the same operation ID; submissions are not auto-retried.

LocalNativeRegistry substitutes production native venue admission and is restricted
at construction to chain 31337. The mock venue/feed/VRF are not Uniswap/Pons or
live price qualification. Production registry pins remain unchanged. Normal
launcher restart creates a new chain; the external one-session recovery scripts
are not a general production recovery facility. Snapshot freshness still samples
actual chain time before and after reads; work deadlines advance monotonically.

Fixed $100 is enforced by the local UI/API; production Entry retains its $100
minimum. Live fixed-value quoting/rounding policy remains an open release task.
No public website/server deployment. Independent audit, production wallet signing,
live routes/feeds and operating qualification remain open. Release NOT APPROVED.

## Internal review and behavior

- **Intent and authority:** strict typed actions, fixed targets/value, exact
  ownership and ordinal/ledger checks; no supplied arbitrary call, recipient,
  chain, approval, nonce or state override. No signer/broadcast API. Simulation
  from a public address does not authenticate its holder; the wallet must sign.
- **Mint controls:** canonical operating state, preparation/global/mint pauses,
  exact supply and price. Full simulation remains required for VRF/recipient
  callbacks; unrelated reward currencies no longer block mint preparation.
- **Claim isolation:** full core and inventory checks remain mandatory. Only
  unselected asset runtime/decimal failures may be isolated. Selected failures,
  malformed inventories, unavailable entitlement or exact-call reverts reject
  the whole draft. WorkLimit is terminal. Claims remain independent of pauses
  while operating; canonical locks cannot be bypassed.
- **Gas and funds:** required policy binds deployment/read configuration and
  reviewed complete fee semantics. Bounds apply to estimate, gas price and
  suggested-limit cost; native payment and gas are separate. Expected claim
  proceeds cannot fund upfront gas. Missing hash-estimation support has no
  latest-state fallback. Gas is a quote, not a guarantee of inclusion cost.
- **Availability:** direct/nested work budgets and stricter snapshot expiry;
  serial supervised HTTP with bounded cleanup. Inputs/results are bounded,
  errors sanitized, read-only default preserved. Reorg/expiry after simulation
  or estimation cannot produce a successful draft.
- **Integration:** actual loopback HTTP request parsing, direct preparer and
  process boundary tests cover their respective layers. These are offline RPC
  fixtures, not a hosted production or browser-wallet rehearsal. Approval,
  signing, account/chain changes and receipt handling remain browser work.

No unauthorized principal path or hidden recipient was added in this scoped
review. This is internal review, not an independent audit or a no-vulnerability
guarantee. Reviewed RPCs may still misreport state; code pins are not consensus
finality proofs. The operator attests fee completeness, and public ingress can
still suffer resource exhaustion without qualified proxy/rate/monitoring controls.
Short expiry is a client rule, not a contract deadline. Frontend revalidation and
receipt/replacement/reorg recovery are required before real wallet use.

# Replacement holder preflight verification

2026-10-19. **Read-only implementation; no production or escrow approval.**

[Twelve targeted Python tests passed](verification.json), no failures or skips.
They exercise confirmed hash reads, source/runtime/NFT binding checks, an optional
distinct inert destination, active/frozen lifecycle, 1,000-NFT paged coverage,
missing/duplicate/mixed/corrupt observations, zero owners, malformed account code,
contract and delegated-account flags, chain/reorg/confirmation rejection and
bounded-work failure. Mock RPC accepts only read methods. No public RPC, deployment,
signer, website/server or monitor was used.

The [tool](../../scripts/inventory-nft-holders.py) and
[implementation](../../zzz_ops/holder_preflight.py) never authorize migration.
The [operator procedure](../../docs/HOLDER_PREFLIGHT.md) requires reviewing exact
replacement withdrawal/claim behavior, resolving incompatible escrows before
freeze, rescanning frozen ownership, and using funded abort before withdrawals
if a problem is discovered after freeze. Retirement remains irreversible.

Internal review checked these boundaries:

- Pages cannot silently fall back to latest reads or combine different snapshots.
  All NFT/owner code reads use the explicit canonical block hash; final header and
  confirmation checks reject a changed anchor. An old snapshot remains historical,
  not automatically valid for committing a handoff.
- A checksum detects accidental file changes, not an adversary forging local
  evidence. This CLI takes trusted operator configuration; providers and reviews
  remain trust boundaries. Use independent evidence for release decisions.
- No-code owners are not declared safe EOAs. Code-bearing owners are always
  unresolved; neither a receiver interface nor a runtime hash proves an escrow
  can release the replacement. Proxy/admin/delegation review remains manual.
- No arbitrary transaction, approval, owner rewrite, NFT transfer or test callback
  is executed. No unreviewed “compatible” flag grants automatic release approval.
- Page bounds, RPC work/time limits and sanitized CLI errors constrain failure.
  Failed reads do not create successful pages; exclusive output creation protects
  previously saved observations. Offline summary makes missing coverage explicit.

Solidity, keeper execution and shared RPC code are unchanged in this follow-up.
Their existing source-bound evidence was reused; no contract regression was
repeated. The preceding [royalty verification](../royalty-conversion/VERIFICATION.md)
remains the latest affected contract evidence. Actual escrow/marketplace operation,
independent review and canonical migration qualification remain open in the
[central Todo](../../TODO.md#task-security-chain-recovery).

## Findings and architectural risks

Severity indicates potential impact under the listed preconditions. A privileged
trust risk is distinguished from an unprivileged exploit. No claim is made that
every possible defect has been found.

| ID | Severity / category | Preconditions and impact | Resolution / evidence boundary |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AE-01 | High availability in the baseline; locally repaired | Governance reserves a pool, then other approved first arrivals fill all four historical slots before delivery. The old implementation rejects the reserved arrival; externally delivered funds may require provider recovery. No incumbent local theft demonstrated. | Permanent idempotent capacity admission is implemented with source-bound regressions. Source still does not verify remote admission proof; external qualification remains a migration release gate. |
| AE-02 | Critical custody trust if maliciously admitted | A correctly pinned approved provider consumes exact principal but does not fund destination. Exact balance depletion and a receipt cannot prove remote custody/backing. | Demonstrative real-router test; keep real bridges disabled. Independently qualify each provider/destination and its administration. No generic local fix proves arbitrary future code honest. |
| AE-03 | High architectural incompatibility | Governance wants ZZZ/WETH -> ZZZ/USDC. Pair guard rejects it; removing that guard would leave immutable old inboxes, home-currency reward paths and v3 liabilities inconsistent. | Preserve rejection; document composition epochs and typed conversion. Implementation requires bounded historical intake/asset obligations and a new authenticated protocol version. |
| AE-04 | Critical catastrophic continuity risk | Canonical home chain permanently stops or cannot process ownership/claims, even while remote LP continues. LP migration leaves canonical NFT and two reward ledgers at home. | User selected planned whole-protocol freeze/export/import while the source works; implementation and finality qualification are pre-seal requirements. Post-halt recovery is deferred; no universal snapshot recovery claim. |
| AE-05 | High economic trust | Governance admits false price feeds, a compromised token/wrapper or harmful routes; keeper repeats permitted lossy operations. Local permission/slippage tests can pass while holders lose value. | Retain bounded parameters and source pins, require feed/admin/venue review and strategy/MEV rehearsals. Record cumulative migration costs. A per-move 3% cap is not profitability or independent oracle truth. |
| AE-06 | High availability | Fixed coordinator fails to fulfill an early ordered VRF request. Later reveals and activation can remain blocked. | Existing tests/source establish ordered dependency; no redundant rerun. Live provider qualification and a fairness-preserving continuity decision remain open; no administrator reroll added. |
| AE-07 | High integration gate, not current simulated-wallet exploit | Live UI adopts Number-based example IDs or trusts unsigned API targets without independent chain/account/identity checks. Hashed uint256 IDs may be rounded; stale or substituted transactions could be signed. | Keep simulation separate. Require exact decimal strings, independent deployment/asset validation, draft expiry, wallet checks and canonical receipt handling. Backend preparation is still unpublished. |
| AE-08 | Medium operating/availability gate | Missing off-host state, competing signer hosts, nonredundant RPC/fee service, missed alerts, provider or token outage. Staging snapshots alone do not prove unattended recovery. | Reuse exact-source keeper evidence; do not equate Anvil/desktop heartbeat with target-chain production or continuous uptime. Distinct-host loss/rotation and real services remain release gates. |

No production rewrite is justified merely because the prompt says "implement" an
already implemented feature. Record any demonstrated new defect and its repair
in the final verification report rather than counting a test as a source fix.

Severity and prerequisites: Q1-Q3 are medium-priority verification gaps, not
demonstrated asset-theft vulnerabilities. R1 is a medium liveness risk conditional
on a previously admitted token failing; healthy assets remain claimable. R2 is a
high-priority blocker **before enabling real cross-chain movement**: competing
admissions can consume capacity before delivery. Migration remains disabled for
initial launch. R3 is a medium functionality limitation when custody stays remote.
R4 requires economic review for low-decimal/high-value assets; repeated boundary
settlement can make a small raw-unit exception material. R5 is execution-order
behavior, not unauthorized claiming. No newly demonstrated critical/high exploit
in the enabled local ownership/reward paths was found; this is not an absence proof.

### AUD18-01 - High-impact accepted trust: immediate governance

[AccessController](../../src/ZZZAccessController.sol) retains role checks, exact
operation hashes, cancellation, predecessor ordering and replay protection, but
its scheduling delay is zero and cannot be increased. The additional migration
waiting period is also zero. This implements the user's explicit policy; it is
not an accidental public authorization bypass.

Compromised or malicious authorized governance can immediately approve harmful
feeds, external dependencies or compatible successor code. The accepted ability
to approve different successor code means that an approved malicious replacement
could divert LP. Code hashes authenticate selected bytes, not their honesty.
Sealing and execution-loss checks cannot compensate for malicious approved
valuation or replacement semantics. A guardian pause is not a veto over governance.

Before release, independently review the actual multisig, signers, role holders,
operation review procedure and dependency/code admission. There is no advance
reaction window. This report does not reinstate a timelock or an identical-code
restriction. Owner: [governance security](../../TODO.md#task-security-governance).

## Implementation and authority

The production behavioral changes are limited to AccessController and Migration.
AccessController retains OpenZeppelin TimelockController's exact operation IDs,
proposer/executor/canceller access checks, rollback, predecessors and replay rules.
Its constructor now rejects nonzero delay; both scheduling overrides reject
nonzero operation delay before calling the unchanged parent implementations.
The existing `updateDelay` override always reverts. Timestamp zero/one are
rejected because OpenZeppelin reserves them for unset/completed operations.

No direct arbitrary governance executor, caller-selected delegatecall, new fast
manager, key, custody recipient or generic upgrade is introduced. The controller
still cannot call as the Vault. Bootstrap revocation, fixed sealed module bindings,
canonical lifecycle guards and guardian/keeper boundaries are unchanged. Open
executor mode executes an approved exact operation, not arbitrary user calldata.

Migration's public delay constant is zero. A plan records its proposal timestamp
as `earliest`; its layout, IDs, snapshot, epoch, status transitions, authorizations
and economic checks are unchanged. Only governance proposes and only an authorized
keeper executes. Timeliness does not replace actual route readiness, current

## Failure isolation and migration

The user explicitly accepted delayed per-currency eligibility. Each optional token
sync has a 250,000-gas self-call boundary, copies no returned failure bytes and can
only be entered by the ledger itself. A gas reserve prevents deliberately starving
the isolated call; overall transaction gas shortages still revert. The total
inventory is bounded by 17 currencies and 1,000 activations. Healthy activation
updates global rarity weight and healthy-asset eligibility; failed assets retain
their earlier cohort and emit a deferred event.

Recovery indexes unseen funds using the earlier eligible weight, then enrolls the
waiting activation interval at that new index. This intentionally includes receipts
arriving during an outage: exact arrival ownership cannot be reconstructed from an
unreadable ERC20 balance. Newly active NFTs receive no retroactive catch-up for
that currency. Empty earlier cohorts quarantine their receipts. Binary searches
over bounded recovery intervals avoid unbounded per-holder synchronization.

Canonical capture still requires readable exact backing. Settlement uses the
earlier asset weight, recovers waiting members, and exports effective per-NFT paid
indices. Import rebuilds activation ordinals and enables the fully settled cohort
on activation. Exported record shapes and classified backing remain unchanged.
Tests cover converted ETH plus remaining token rights through export/import as
well as existing full handoff and abort tests. This is same-chain evidence only.

## Result and accounting

One stable bucket owns one physical LP position per registered pool/strategy. NFTs hold canonical nonredeemable shares and retain individual funded fee balances. Harvest, compounding and rebalancing act once per bucket, without iterating over NFT holders. Contribution, custody and reward ledgers remain separate.

Paid dormant minting remains exactly 0.05 ETH and creates no LP, Power or fees. Activation requires at least $500 of net new, measured deployed LP, conservatively excluding incumbent idle and fresh compounding value. Permanent top-ups buy shares against current incumbent NAV rather than historical contributions. Zero NAV with outstanding shares, zero issuance and supply above 1e36 revert.

Entry harvests earlier fees and entry-swap fees before shares change. Existing LP quantities are valued again after balancing so their repricing stays with incumbents. Owner checkpoints precede share changes; collective checkpoints precede Power changes. The owner allocation follows bucket shares, collective rewards follow lifetime contribution Power, and only the designated 10% compounds. Donations and the other fee reserves cannot become share-purchase principal. NFT transfers preserve shares and unclaimed rights; claims work while maintenance is paused.

Whole-bucket version-3 migrations preserve canonical membership and Power, freeze new shares while scheduled/remote, and carry cumulative remote owner/collective allocations including unsent reserves. A home return cannot admit new shares or release principal again until all those old allocations are funded home. Maintenance, transfers and funded claims remain possible. Destination pools require permanent reservations; distinct buckets cannot merge implicitly. Repeated A->B->C->A->B and return/new-join/revisit scenarios pass with a real controller/router and mock provider.

The former `position(nftId)` ABI is removed. NFT consumers read `nftStatus`, `nftBucket`, `sharesOf`, `contributionUSD` and Rewards; physical custody comes from `group(bucketId)`. Maintenance IDs and fee-controller IDs are buckets. `bucketCount/bucketAt` provide bounded keeper discovery with a durable fair cursor. ## Three distinct funding paths

```text
Conventional v4 LP fees -> LiquidityManager.collect -> Vault fee deltas
                                                         |
Creator's actual payment -> immutable RewardReceiver.sync |
                              -> FeeController.allocateExternal
                                                         |
                                              FeeController
                      +----------------+-----------------+-------------+
                      |                |                 |             |
                    80%              10%                 5%            5%
             bucket owner index   equal NFT index    bucket compound  buyback
                      +------ Rewards ------+          reserve        reserve
                                  |                       |             |
                        current-owner claims        permanent LP   swap + burn

Marketplace royalty actually received -> NFT.royaltyRewards()
                                      -> separate 1/2/3 index
                                      -> current-owner royalty claim
```

The selected native-ETH/Pons market has zero conventional LP fees in the reviewed
configuration. Its creator/hook revenue is a distinct stream. Holding liquidity
does not itself authorize PoPL to debit the creator or receive that revenue.
The agreement's basis, share, assets and frequency remain to be finalized.

FeeController allocates only pulled, funded assets. Native creator payments need
the admitted wrapper and become the canonical pair asset. Ordinary pair receipts
are forwarded through the fixed bucket inbox. Mint proceeds, old idle principal,
LP removal proceeds, unattributed donations and royalty balances are not LP fees.
Satellite owner/collective reserves return as already allocated 90% funds, with
provenance and funded-liability checks; they are not split a second time.

The 80% owner index is bucket-specific and proportional to LP shares. The 10%
collective index gives each activated canonical NFT one equal share. Rarity has
no influence on either. Funded dust and pending local creator inboxes settle
before new membership. Top-ups checkpoint old shares first and add no membership.

The 5% compound reserve belongs to the earning bucket. Only the Vault may consume
it into its attributed idle/deployed principal. The keeper cannot receive it.
The 5% buyback reserve is segregated by asset; the fixed Buyback module obtains
only its recorded budget, uses an admitted direct pair or burns ZZZ directly,
then checks both supply reduction and its remaining ZZZ balance. Failed execution
must atomically restore reserves and keep unrelated funded claims available.
Price/slippage/deadline checks limit execution; they do not eliminate MEV or IL.

Royalties are allocated separately when admitted funds are observed. Pending
receipts synchronize before activation or claim. Prefunds, pre-admission balances
and receipts with no eligible NFTs remain quarantined. Fractional and global
division dust stays backed; no administrator can sweep it. Native ETH and
admitted exact-transfer ERC20 assets have independent accounting and units.

## Residual risks and release requirements

- **Independence is not provable from addresses.** Two providers can share an
  administrator or the same thin underlying market. If both agree on a wrong
  price, two-of-two consensus cannot identify it. The governance review hash and
  independence labels record assertions; they are not cryptographic market truth.
- **Source/proxy administration matters.** A stable proxy runtime does not pin
  its implementation or upstream reporters. Qualify source-specific authorities,
  implementation/configuration checks and continuous operating monitoring.
- **Availability is deliberately conservative.** Either invalid source blocks
  price-dependent contributions. Source replacement is governed; no stale or
  one-source fallback exists. Funded claims and applicable raw custody recovery
  remain independent of pricing; unusable venues/tokens can still prevent exit.
- **Actual market value is not guaranteed.** Raw LP units/inventory are facts;
  USD value depends on the source assumptions. These guards do not remove market
  movement, impermanent loss or permitted MEV/execution cost.
- **Real services are not selected.** ETH, ZZZ, USDG and any admitted USDC input
  need independently qualified source pairs, ages, routes and market depth.
  Creator/team input cannot substitute for that qualification.
- **Capacity qualification remains bounded.** The helper permits 34 distinct
  marks; the current read/preflight inventory supports 33 priced assets. An
  extreme configuration beyond that profile must fail closed until reviewed.

## 4. Assess the overlapping financial check precisely

The pre-mint whole-idle-budget check is `Budget.assertIdleLoss` in Vault
`_redeploy`. Activation/growth use a separate entrant path and actual marginal
LP guards; contribution2% is not this pool's slippage setting. The fresh

For ordinary zero/one-swap balancing, fixed marks and ignoring integer rounding,
let B be the lower-USD whole idle budget, I<=B the lower-USD swapped input,
U>=I its upper-USD mark, t the target fractional allowance, v the venue allowance
and s=min(t,v). O is lower-USD actual output. Exact swap guards imply

budget cap while bypassing the ordinary helper's tighter-target comparison;

source-exact rounding/control proof for any proposed normal-path consolidation.

## Final publication review: deferred native credit guard

The new rejection of a nonzero **available** native claimable balance on a
native-ineligible active NFT was independently traced again before publication.
No legitimate counterexample was found in the current pinned operating ledger:

- Activation is one-time (`ZZZRoyaltyRewards.sol:196–220`). A native-deferred
  NFT is a new activation whose ordinal exceeds the native eligible prefix;
  existing eligible NFTs never lose eligibility when another custody episode
  begins (`eligibleFor`/`_enrollWaiting`, lines 231–238). It therefore cannot
  bring previously earned native credit into a newly deferred state.
- Ordinary royalty accrual uses weight zero for an ineligible currency
  (`_checkpoint`, lines 330–339). Plain ETH receipts create pending raw funds,
  not an `accrued` balance for the newcomer. During actual custody, the native
  `claimable` view reverts; after exact return but before sync it returns the
  newcomer's zero stored accrual (lines 376–385).
- Conversion does credit ETH directly at line 166, but first calls `_sync(0)`
  at line 142. That call rejects active native custody at line 295; after return
  it allocates older pending receipts and enrolls waiting NFTs before any native
  conversion credit is assigned. Conversion also rejects never-activated NFTs
  at line 146. Thus a successful conversion cannot leave credited ETH on an NFT
  that is still outside the native prefix.
- Complete handoff cannot capture outstanding royalty custody (line 403).
  Settlement enrolls waiting currencies before export (lines 418–428), and
  destination activation sets every admitted currency's prefix/weight to all
  imported active NFTs (lines 495–501). Import may transiently hold nonzero
  accrued amounts before eligibility initialization, but that is an importing
  deployment, not a supported holdings projection: `Projection._verify_deployment`
  rejects non-operating lifecycle states at `service.py:315–317`, before
  `Projection.nft` calls royalty reporting.

This argument depends on the current pinned ledger, monotonic one-time
activation and the API's operating-lifecycle guard. It must be revisited if
another implementation adds direct native-credit writers, eligibility removal
or read access to importing states. It does not claim arbitrary replacement
code can satisfy the same invariant. The final backend diff also retains strict
custody-event layouts, admitted currencies, emitter identity, exact return IDs/
amounts, deferred-prefix checks and existing request-budget propagation. The
three conditional native-custody proof reads are bounded and use the original
typed block-pinned read helper; no retry, write or signing path is added.
